
```{r}
library(mini007)

retrieve_open_ai_credential <- function() {
  Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
}

openai_4_1_mini <- ellmer::chat(
  name = "openai/gpt-4.1-mini",
  credentials = retrieve_open_ai_credential,
  echo = "none"
)
```

By default, agents start every task from scratch: a `LeadAgent` picks an
agent for a subtask from its instruction alone, and nothing that went well or
badly in a previous run informs the next one. A `Memory` changes that. It
stores what agents learned from past tasks and feeds it back into future
ones, within a session or across sessions.

How it works:

- **Judge.** Every delegated step is scored from 0 to 1 against criteria you
  set. A step that scores too low is handed to another agent, and the best
  attempt is kept.
- **Remember.** Each judged step is recorded as an *outcome* (who did what,
  and how well), and the same judging call distills a short, reusable
  *lesson* from it. Human edits at a HITL step are remembered too.
- **Reuse.** When choosing an agent, the `LeadAgent` sees each agent's track
  record. When delegating a task, the lessons most relevant to it are added to
  the prompt.
- **Persist.** Give the `Memory` a file path and all of this carries over to
  the next R session.

## A quality gate for LeadAgent

`$set_validation()` makes the `LeadAgent` check every response it receives
from a sub-agent. Responses scoring below `threshold` are reassigned to the
next best agent, up to `max_reassign` times.

```{r}
researcher <- Agent$new(
  name = "researcher",
  instruction = "You answer factual questions in at most 2 lines, in English only.",
  llm_object = openai_4_1_mini
)

translator <- Agent$new(
  name = "translator",
  instruction = "You translate English text to German. Return only the translation.",
  llm_object = openai_4_1_mini
)

lead_agent <- LeadAgent$new(name = "Leader", llm_object = openai_4_1_mini)
lead_agent$register_agents(c(researcher, translator))

lead_agent$set_validation(
  criteria = "Accurate, complete, and in the language the task asks for.",
  threshold = 0.7,
  max_reassign = 1
)
```

Each step in `agents_interaction` now carries its `score`, its `feedback`, and
every `attempts` made:

```{r}
answer <- lead_agent$invoke(
  "Give the capital of Algeria and its population in one sentence, answered in German."
)
answer

for (step in lead_agent$agents_interaction) {
  cat(step$agent_name, "| score:", step$score, "|", step$feedback, "\n\n")
}
```

While streaming, validation shows up as `"task_validated"` events, and a
reassignment as a `"task_reassigned"` event (see the
[Streaming](streaming.html) article).

## Remembering outcomes and lessons

Attach a `Memory` with `$set_memory()`. With validation on, the lead agent now
also learns from every step it judges:

```{r}
memory_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")

lead_agent$set_memory(Memory$new(path = memory_path))

answer <- lead_agent$invoke(
  "Name the longest river in Africa and its length in one sentence, answered in German."
)
answer
```

Each agent now has a track record. It is shown to the LLM whenever the lead
agent chooses who should handle a subtask, so agents that did well on similar
tasks are preferred and those that failed them are avoided:

```{r}
lead_agent$agent_track_record()
```

And each judged step left a lesson behind:

```{r}
for (lesson in lead_agent$memory$lessons) {
  cat("-", lesson$agent_name, ":", lesson$lesson, "\n")
}
```

The next time a task resembles one of these, the most relevant lessons
(3 by default, set with `$set_memory(memory, k = )`) are placed in front of
the task sent to the agent, under a "Lessons learned from previous similar
tasks" heading. `$search()` shows which ones a task would get:

```{r}
lessons <- lead_agent$memory$search("Translate a short answer into German")
for (lesson in lessons) cat("-", lesson$lesson, "\n")
```

Lessons are ranked by keyword relevance (BM25), which needs no extra
dependency. To use another retriever, e.g. one based on embeddings, pass
`search_fn = function(query, lessons, k)` to `Memory$new()`.

Learning adds no LLM call to a validated step: the score, the feedback and the
lesson come from the same request.

## Learning from humans

When a `Memory` is attached, the decisions made at an HITL step (see
`$set_hitl()`) are recorded as outcomes as well: accepting a response counts
as a success, editing or stopping it as a failure. An edit is the most
informative signal there is, so it is also distilled into a lesson that
describes what the human changed.

## Across sessions

A `Memory` created with a `path` is saved after every change and loaded again
when you create it with the same path, so a new session starts with
everything learned before:

```{r}
memory <- Memory$new(path = memory_path)
cat(length(memory$lessons), "lessons and", length(memory$outcomes), "outcomes reloaded\n")
```

The file is plain JSON, so lessons can be read, edited, or removed by hand.
`$max_lessons` and `$max_outcomes` (500 and 1000 by default) cap its size by
dropping the oldest records first, and `$clear()` empties it.

Several agents can share the same `Memory` object, and a clone made with
`$clone_agent()` keeps using the memory of its original.

## A single Agent

An `Agent` can learn on its own too. `$learn()` takes the result of
`$validate_response()`, records the outcome and stores a lesson; from then
on, `$invoke()` adds the relevant lessons in front of each prompt.

```{r}
fact_checker <- Agent$new(
  name = "fact_checker",
  instruction = "You are a factual assistant. Answer in one sentence.",
  llm_object = openai_4_1_mini
)

fact_checker$set_memory(Memory$new())

prompt <- "When did Algeria gain its independence?"
response <- fact_checker$invoke(prompt)

validation <- fact_checker$validate_response(
  prompt = prompt,
  response = response,
  validation_criteria = "Gives the exact date (day, month and year)."
)

fact_checker$learn(validation)

fact_checker$memory$lessons[[1]]$lesson
```

## Reference

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `Memory$new(path, max_lessons, max_outcomes, search_fn)` | Create a memory, loaded from `path` if it exists |
| `$add_lesson()` / `$add_outcome()` | Store a lesson or an outcome by hand |
| `$search(query, k, agent_name)` | The lessons most relevant to `query` |
| `$track_record(agent_names)` | Outcomes summarised per agent |
| `$save()` / `$load()` / `$clear()` | Persistence |
| `Agent$set_memory(memory, k)` | Attach a memory to an Agent or LeadAgent |
| `Agent$learn(validation)` | Learn from a `$validate_response()` result |
| `LeadAgent$set_validation(criteria, threshold, max_reassign)` | Judge, reassign and learn from every delegated step |
| `LeadAgent$agent_track_record()` | Track record of every registered agent |
